bottlenecks.description: Explainability requirements for ML-based CDSS create tension between model complexity and clinical interpretability, with regulatory implications

np_hard_problems.problem: Clinical pathway scheduling and resource allocation - optimizing patient flow through treatment activities with constrained resources (staff, equipment, beds)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reduction from job shop scheduling); strongly NP-hard for block scheduling variants
current_approaches: Hybrid genetic algorithms with particle swarm optimization
Timed continuous Petri nets (TCPNs) for pathway modeling
Stochastic process algebra (PEPA) for performance analysis
Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) for radiotherapy scheduling
Column generation approaches for radiation therapy patient scheduling
gaps: Exact solutions computationally infeasible for real-world hospital scale
Stochastic patient arrival and service times not fully captured
Multi-objective optimization (patient wait time, resource utilization, clinical outcomes) remains challenging

np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal antibiotic treatment planning (Antibiotics Time Machine) - finding optimal sequence of antibiotics to minimize resistance
current_approaches: Exhaustive enumeration for small instances (up to 6 antibiotics)
gaps: No polynomial-time algorithm exists for general case
Combinatorial explosion with number of antibiotics and treatment length

np_hard_problems.problem: Drug combination optimization - selecting optimal subset of drugs maximizing synergy while minimizing adverse interactions
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (equivalent to maximum independent set / QUBO formulations)
current_approaches: Feedback system control (FSC) for iterative optimization
Two-step optimization: regimen selection then dose optimization
Literature data mining for candidate pre-selection
gaps: 20-50 drug libraries yield >60,000 possible regimens of 2-6 drugs
Dose-dependent interactions not captured by pairwise models
Clinical validation of computationally optimized combinations remains expensive

np_hard_problems.problem: K-adaptability in robust treatment planning - computing K treatment plans in advance for proton therapy under uncertainty
current_approaches: Two-phase heuristic: scenario clustering then plan redistribution
gaps: Clinical implementation requires real-time plan selection
Uncertainty sets grow exponentially with number of scenarios

failure_modes.mode: Alert fatigue and desensitization - clinicians override 49-96% of alerts due to excessive false positives, potentially missing critical warnings
failure_modes.mitigation: Reduce within-patient repeats, incorporate patient-specific characteristics, use noninterruptive alert formats, monitor provider alert exposure

failure_modes.mode: Automation bias - clinicians over-rely on CDSS recommendations without independent verification
failure_modes.mitigation: Design for independent review of recommendation basis, present options rather than directives, maintain clinician autonomy in decision-making

failure_modes.mode: Data quality and completeness issues - missing or incorrect EHR data leads to inappropriate recommendations
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement data validation pipelines, flag missing data in CDSS output, use probabilistic reasoning under uncertainty

failure_modes.mode: Model drift and performance degradation - ML models degrade over time as patient populations and clinical practices change
failure_modes.mitigation: Continuous monitoring of model performance, periodic retraining, predetermined change control plans (PCCP)

failure_modes.mode: Workflow integration failure - CDSS recommendations not aligned with clinical workflow timing and context
failure_modes.mitigation: User-centered design process, CDS Hooks for event-triggered delivery, integration testing in real clinical environments

failure_modes.mode: Bias and fairness failures - models trained on non-representative data produce inequitable recommendations
failure_modes.mitigation: Fairness assessment methodology documentation (HTI-1 requirement), diverse training data, bias testing across demographic groups

hardware_requirements.minimum: CPU-only: 4-8 cores, 16-32GB RAM for rule-based CDSS and small ML models (tabular GBM, small CNNs); edge devices like Raspberry Pi 4 viable for tabular models
hardware_requirements.recommended: GPU-accelerated: NVIDIA RTX 3090/4090 or A10 for deep learning inference; 24GB+ VRAM for transformer models; edge deployment on Jetson AGX Orin for real-time applications

scalability_limits.limit: Concurrent user sessions for EHR-embedded CDSS
scalability_limits.threshold: 1,500+ concurrent users typical for hospital information systems; CDSS must maintain <200ms response time at peak load

scalability_limits.limit: Real-time inference throughput for continuous monitoring
scalability_limits.threshold: 1,500 scoring requests per 15-minute window for 430-bed hospital; 300 inferences/second per GPU node
Sub-10ms required for 250Hz multi-lead ECG processing; only GPU/edge accelerators meet this requirement
5-200 hospitals: convergence time 48-68 rounds; AUROC degradation 0-1.3% vs centralized baseline
NP-hard scheduling becomes intractable beyond ~50 activities with multiple resources; heuristics required for real-world scale
20-50 drug libraries yield >60,000 regimens of 2-6 drugs; brute-force screening impracticable beyond 10 drugs

regulations: FDA Section 520(o)(1)(E) - 21st Century Cures Act CDS exclusion (four-criteria test)
FDA Clinical Decision Support Software Guidance (January 2026)
ONC HTI-1 Final Rule (89 FR 1192, effective February 8, 2024) - Decision Support Interventions criterion at 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11)
HIPAA Privacy and Security Rule for PHI protection
HTI-5 proposed rule (December 2025) - would remove model card requirements for predictive DSIs
21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
GDPR for European patient data protection
challenges: Transparency vs performance tradeoff: opaque ML models may fail FDA Criterion 4 (independent review requirement)
Time-critical CDS (sepsis alerts, arrhythmia detection) generally cannot meet Criterion 4 and remain regulated devices
HTI-1 requires 31 source attributes for predictive DSIs vs 13 for evidence-based DSIs
Information blocking regulations create tension with proprietary CDS algorithms
Liability allocation between CDS vendors, healthcare providers, and clinicians remains unclear
Model validation requirements: external validation, fairness assessment, ongoing performance monitoring
Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) required for AI/ML-based CDS updates

cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Superior predictive performance for complex patterns; automatic feature learning; continuous improvement with data

cost_tradeoffs.cost: Communication overhead for model synchronization; complexity of differential privacy implementation; convergence challenges with heterogeneous data
